leads.summary: #10162's Hyprland exec-rule repair is bypassed by the new autostart route after both PRs merge
leads.consequence: #10162 teaches o.launch to transform [float] kitty into [float] uwsm-app -- kitty. Prior to this PR o.launch_on_start delegated to o.launch, but the new route passes [float] to omarchy-launch-autostart as its first app argument. The helper forwards that to uwsm-app -- [float] kitty; UWSM treats [float] as the binary and rejects it. On the current quattro tip plus both independent PRs the merge has no conflict markers, both reviewed autostart tests and bin style pass, but the merged Lua invocation prints startup: omarchy-launch-autostart [float] kitty versus direct: [float] uwsm-app -- kitty. leads.summary: Connection and option errors are logged as a 15-second notification-service timeout
leads.consequence: gdbus wait returns failure before starting its 15-second timer if it cannot connect to the session bus (or rejects an invalid option). The helper discards stderr and unconditionally logs 'did not appear within 15s' for every nonzero, then launches the app. On a transient missing bus this creates a misleading diagnosis of slow login and omits the actual transport failure even though the app starts immediately. Preserve or classify the error before claiming a timeout, or state only that the wait failed. A sandboxed bus-error fake produced the exact misleading line and exit 0; source inspection verifies real gdbus's immediate error path.

leads.summary: The Sunshine installer is an in-repository non-notification autostart caller subject to the blanket delay
leads.consequence: When the installer reaches its final enable_hyprland_autostart, it writes o.launch_on_start("sunshine") after separately enabling and starting the Sunshine user service. If org.freedesktop.Notifications is absent, this redundant launcher now waits up to 15 seconds, while the systemd unit starts separately; in configurations where the separate unit does not work, the Hyprland fallback is also delayed. The installer already has a duplicate-start defect, addressed in open #12472/#12358. This PR need not fix that defect, but the blanket wait has a concrete first-party caller despite the description's 'no entry needs to move' premise. A surgical exception for non-notification services or coordination with either Sunshine fix avoids imposing startup latency for this entry; it does not imply the normal working systemd unit is delayed.

leads.summary: Manual promises the Omarchy shell is ready although the wait accepts any owner of the Notifications name
leads.consequence: If another notification daemon owns org.freedesktop.Notifications, gdbus wait returns success even when the Omarchy notifications plugin is disabled or Omarchy's shell is not running. Autostart apps then use that daemon, rather than necessarily sending through Omarchy as the new manual claims; the disabled-plugin case need not cost 15 seconds. ## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Combined with open PR #10162, `[workspace N]` rules in `autostart.lua` (issue #10137) would stay broken, because `o.launch_on_start` no longer goes through the fixed `o.launch`.

### Autostart entries bypass the #10162 exec-rule fix

#10162 fixes `o.launch_on_start("[workspace 4 silent] foot")` inside `o.launch`. This PR stops routing `o.launch_on_start` through `o.launch`, so with both merged the exec string is `omarchy-launch-autostart [workspace 4 silent] foot` and `uwsm-app` again gets `[workspace` as the program. **Impact:** the two diffs apply cleanly and both PRs' tests pass, so nothing flags it.

**Suggested change:** in `o.launch_on_start`, keep a leading `[...]` block in front of `omarchy-launch-autostart`, as #10162 does in `o.launch`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at f61bc17 and with #10162 plus this PR; passes with #10162 alone)</summary>

# o.launch_on_start no longer goes through o.launch, so the #10162 exec-rule fix stops reaching autostart

Reviewed head: f61bc176e9911a67f5dd255a43b2ed3478a55f49. Other trees: `quattro` at b421b1b479ee9ea0863792282eee4ffeb50923dc, and open PR #10162 at 0f76e7ec43b70ac6f3370c73181d15d28f4fecd2.

Issue #10137 reports that `o.launch_on_start("[workspace 2 silent] some-app")` never opens a window, because `uwsm-app` receives `[workspace` as the program name. Open PR #10162 fixes it inside `o.launch` by keeping a leading `[...]` block in front of `uwsm-app --`. Before this PR, `o.launch_on_start` called `o.launch`, so it picked up that fix. With this PR it builds `"omarchy-launch-autostart " .. command` itself, so the rule block goes back to being an argument to `uwsm-app`.

The two PRs touch different lines of `default/hypr/helpers.lua`. Applied together on `quattro` (`git apply` of the #10162 diff, then of this PR's diff) both applied cleanly. #10162's own `test/shell.d/hyprland-launch-test.sh` and this PR's `test/shell.d/launch-autostart-test.sh` both pass on the combined tree, so nothing flags the interaction.

## Test (drop into `test/shell.d/`, same style as the PR's test)

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

require_command lua

# The string the hyprland.start handler hands to hl.exec_cmd for an autostart
# entry that carries a Hyprland exec rule.
output=$(OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" lua <<'LUA'
package.path = os.getenv("OMARCHY_PATH") .. "/?.lua;" .. package.path
local handlers, executed = {}, {}
hl = {
  on = function(event, fn)
    handlers[event] = handlers[event] or {}
    table.insert(handlers[event], fn)
  end,
  exec_cmd = function(command) table.insert(executed, command) end,
}
require("default.hypr.helpers")
o.launch_on_start("[workspace 4 silent] foot")
for _, fn in ipairs(handlers["hyprland.start"] or {}) do fn() end
print(executed[1])
LUA
) || fail "helpers.lua can be evaluated"

printf 'exec string: %s\n' "$output"
[[ $output == "[workspace 4 silent] "* ]] ||
  fail "o.launch_on_start keeps a Hyprland exec-rule prefix in front of the launch" "$output"
pass "o.launch_on_start keeps a Hyprland exec-rule prefix in front of the launch"
```

```
uwsm-app -- [workspace 4 silent] foot
not ok - o.launch_on_start keeps a Hyprland exec-rule prefix in front of the launch
```

`quattro` + #10162, exit 0:

```
ok - o.launch_on_start keeps a Hyprland exec-rule prefix in front of the launch
```

This PR's head, exit 1:

```
exec string: omarchy-launch-autostart [workspace 4 silent] foot
omarchy-launch-autostart [workspace 4 silent] foot
not ok - o.launch_on_start keeps a Hyprland exec-rule prefix in front of the launch
```

`quattro` + #10162 + this PR, exit 1:

```
exec string: omarchy-launch-autostart [workspace 4 silent] foot
omarchy-launch-autostart [workspace 4 silent] foot
not ok - o.launch_on_start keeps a Hyprland exec-rule prefix in front of the launch
```

What `uwsm-app` then receives on the combined tree. This is an excerpt from a separate harness run, not from the test above: it runs each exec string through Hyprland's `[rules]` stripping (`spawnWithRules` in Hyprland 0.56.2 `Executor.cpp`) and `/bin/sh -c`, with `uwsm-app` stubbed to record its arguments; the `sh-exit 0` line that follows each case is omitted here:

```
== case-9 q10162: [workspace 4 silent] uwsm-app -- app1
   hyprland-exec-rule <workspace 4 silent>
   uwsm-app <--> <app1>
== case-9 both: omarchy-launch-autostart [workspace 4 silent] app1
   gdbus <wait> <--session> <--timeout> <15> <org.freedesktop.Notifications>
   uwsm-app <--> <[workspace> <4> <silent]> <app1>
```

## Notes for a fix

Whichever PR lands second needs to keep a leading `[...]` block in front of `omarchy-launch-autostart` too, for example by splitting it off in `o.launch_on_start` the same way #10162 does in `o.launch`. Hyprland keeps an exec rule for one minute (`IRule::markAsExecRule` sets `expiresAt` to now plus one minute in `src/desktop/rule/Rule.cpp`, v0.56.2) and matches the window by the exec token in its environment or by PID, so a wait of up to 15 s should still fit. That last point is from source only; it was not run in Hyprland.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings: with the notifications plugin off, entries can wait 15 s for nothing</summary>

#### With the notifications plugin off, entries can wait 15 s for nothing

`gdbus wait` without `--activate` never starts a D-Bus-activatable daemon (mako, dunst and swaync ship one for this name). **Impact:** when the daemon is only D-Bus activated or is itself started with `o.launch_on_start`, each entry waits the full 15 s, then the app activates the daemon itself as before; a daemon started with `o.launch_on_start` waits for its own name, so the race returns. An already running daemon ends the wait at once.

**Suggested change:** skip the wait when `shell.json` lists `omarchy.notifications` in `disabledPlugins`, or document the no-wait form for notification daemons.

**Reproducer (private D-Bus, at f61bc17):**

# With the notifications plugin off, the wait never helps: activatable daemons are not started, and a daemon in autostart.lua waits for itself

Reviewed head: f61bc176e9911a67f5dd255a43b2ed3478a55f49

`bin/omarchy-launch-autostart` runs `gdbus wait --session --timeout 15 org.freedesktop.Notifications` without `--activate`. In GLib (`gio/gdbus-tool.c`, `handle_wait`, identical in 2.84.4, 2.86.0 and main) that watches the name with `G_BUS_NAME_WATCHER_FLAGS_NONE`, so D-Bus activation never starts anything; it only returns early if something else claims the name. mako, dunst and SwayNotificationCenter all ship a D-Bus service file with `Name=org.freedesktop.Notifications` (`fr.emersion.mako.service.in`, `org.knopwob.dunst.service.in`, `services/dbus/org.erikreider.swaync.service.in`), and Chromium's own start-up check (`dbus_utils::CheckForServiceAndStart`: NameHasOwner, then ListActivatableNames, then StartServiceByName) activates such a daemon itself.

So for someone who turned off the shell's notifications plugin (`disabledPlugins[]` in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json`) and uses one of those daemons:

- If the daemon is only D-Bus activated and nothing else calls it first, every `o.launch_on_start` entry now waits the full 15 s at login, then the app activates the daemon itself, exactly as it did immediately before this PR. (Only this case was run: nothing else on the private bus called the name.)
- If the daemon is started from `autostart.lua` with `o.launch_on_start`, it waits 15 s for the name it will claim itself, then starts at the same moment as every other entry, so the start-up race this PR removes comes back.

## Script

Save this as `autostart-wait-daemon-repro.sh` and run it from a checkout of the PR head. It needs `dbus-daemon`, `dbus-run-session`, `dbus-send`, `dbus-test-tool` and `gdbus`, and uses private session buses; `uwsm-app` and `logger` are stubs that print a line and then run the command. `dbus-test-tool` stands in for the daemon.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from an Omarchy checkout of the PR head. Needs dbus-daemon, dbus-run-session,
# dbus-send, dbus-test-tool and gdbus. Uses a private session bus; nothing reaches
# the real bus or journal (uwsm-app and logger are stubs that print, then run).
set -uo pipefail

root=$(pwd)
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$work/bin" "$work/services"
name=org.freedesktop.Notifications

cat >"$work/bin/uwsm-app" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
awk -v t="$(date +%s.%N)" -v t0="$T0" -v a="$*" 'BEGIN { printf "   +%.1fs uwsm-app %s\n", t - t0, a }'
shift
exec "$@"
EOF
cat >"$work/bin/logger" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
awk -v t="$(date +%s.%N)" -v t0="$T0" -v a="$*" 'BEGIN { printf "   +%.1fs logger %s\n", t - t0, a }'
EOF
# What Chromium checks once at start: NameHasOwner, then ListActivatableNames,
# then StartServiceByName when the name is activatable.
cat >"$work/bin/probe" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
owner=\$(dbus-send --session --print-reply=literal --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner string:$name | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ //')
if [[ \$owner != "boolean true" ]] && dbus-send --session --print-reply=literal --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus org.freedesktop.DBus.ListActivatableNames | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -Fxq $name; then
  dbus-send --session --print-reply=literal --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus org.freedesktop.DBus.StartServiceByName string:$name uint32:0 >/dev/null
  owner="activated, now \$(dbus-send --session --print-reply=literal --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner string:$name | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ //')"
fi
awk -v t="\$(date +%s.%N)" -v t0="\$T0" -v a="probe[\$1]: notification service at start: \$owner" 'BEGIN { printf "   +%.1fs %s\\n", t - t0, a }'
EOF
# Stand-in for mako/dunst/swaync, which all ship a D-Bus service file for this name.
cat >"$work/bin/notification-daemon" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="\${DBUS_STARTER_ADDRESS:-\$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS}"
exec dbus-test-tool echo --session --name=$name
EOF
chmod +x "$work/bin"/*

bus_config() {
  cat <<EOF
<!DOCTYPE busconfig PUBLIC "-//freedesktop//DTD D-Bus Bus Configuration 1.0//EN"
 "http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/dbus/1.0/busconfig.dtd">
<busconfig>
  <type>session</type>
  <listen>unix:tmpdir=$work</listen>
  $1
  <policy context="default">
    <allow send_destination="*" eavesdrop="true"/>
    <allow eavesdrop="true"/>
    <allow own="*"/>
  </policy>
</busconfig>
EOF
}
bus_config "" >"$work/plain.conf"
printf '[D-BUS Service]\nName=%s\nExec=%s/bin/notification-daemon\n' "$name" "$work" >"$work/services/notifications.service"
bus_config "<servicedir>$work/services</servicedir>" >"$work/activatable.conf"

export PATH="$work/bin:$root/bin:$PATH"

echo "1. Activatable notification daemon installed, not running yet"
echo "   a) launched the pre-PR way (uwsm-app directly):"
dbus-run-session --config-file="$work/activatable.conf" -- bash -c 'export T0=$(date +%s.%N); uwsm-app -- probe direct'
echo "   b) launched through omarchy-launch-autostart:"
dbus-run-session --config-file="$work/activatable.conf" -- bash -c 'export T0=$(date +%s.%N); omarchy-launch-autostart probe helper'

echo "2. The notification daemon is itself an o.launch_on_start entry, next to an app"
dbus-run-session --config-file="$work/plain.conf" -- bash -c '
  export T0=$(date +%s.%N)
  omarchy-launch-autostart notification-daemon &
  daemon=$!
  omarchy-launch-autostart probe app
  kill "$daemon"
'
```

## Actual output

Run with `bash autostart-wait-daemon-repro.sh` from the PR head checkout, exit status 0:

```
1. Activatable notification daemon installed, not running yet
   a) launched the pre-PR way (uwsm-app directly):
   +0.0s uwsm-app -- probe direct
   +0.0s probe[direct]: notification service at start: activated, now boolean true
   b) launched through omarchy-launch-autostart:
   +15.4s logger -t omarchy-autostart org.freedesktop.Notifications did not appear within 15s; launching probe without it.
```

Case 1 follows from the GLib source above rather than from timing: the helper waits the whole timeout, and the probe then activates the daemon itself, which it did at once without the helper.

Case 2 is a race. In this run the daemon claimed the name just before the app's check. In an earlier run of the same shape (the daemon and a Chromium-style probe each launched through the unmodified helper on a private bus), the app checked before the daemon had claimed the name and found no service, which Chromium's native check keeps for the rest of its process:

```
1790699578.350633378 logger <-t>1790699578.350666148 logger <omarchy-autostart> <org.freedesktop.Notifications did not appear within 15s; launching chromium-probe without it.>
 <-t> <omarchy-autostart> <org.freedesktop.Notifications did not appear within 15s; launching fake-notification-daemon without it.>
1790699578.352465011 uwsm-app1790699578.352471698 uwsm-app <--> <chromium-probe> <s5>
 <--> <fake-notification-daemon>
1790699578.353956092 fake-notification-daemon starting
1790699578.356884381 chromium-probe[s5] owner-at-start=boolean false activatable=no => native notifications unavailable for this process lifetime
```

That is the raw call log: the first four lines are interleaved because both helpers timed out and wrote at the same instant. Both launches came 15.62 s after the helpers started; the daemon there is `dbus-test-tool echo --session --name=org.freedesktop.Notifications`.

The other timings measured with the same private bus: name already owned 0.01 s, name claimed after 2 s 2.01 s, name never claimed 14.80 s with exactly one `omarchy-autostart` journal line per entry, three entries in parallel 15.38 s in total.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**

- The argv reaching `uwsm-app` is identical at base and head for 10 quoting and shell-syntax cases, including `o.launch_webapp`, `&&`, `$HOME` and quoted arguments.
- Real `gdbus wait` on a private bus returns after 0.01 s when the name is owned and at 2.01 s when it appears after 2 s; when it never appears, the app launches after about 15 s with one `omarchy-autostart` journal line per entry.
- A config reload dispatches `config.reloaded`, not `hyprland.start` (Hyprland 0.56.2 source), so the wait does not rerun. No first-party default uses `o.launch_on_start`, and the shell starts through `hl.exec_cmd`, so it never waits for itself.
- The new test fails at the merge-base and catches 4 of 9 mutants tried; the other five are optional notes 1 and 2. `test/shell`, the bin style test and the CLI metadata lint show no new failures at the head or on `quattro` with the PR applied.

**Optional notes**

1. The two `helpers.lua` checks are `grep -F` on the source: reverting `o.launch_on_start` while keeping the routing line as a comment passes all nine checks. Evaluating `helpers.lua` with a stub `hl`, as `hyprland-default-config-test.sh` does, catches it.
2. The `gdbus` fake records `"$*"`, so a helper that passes `"--timeout 15"` as one argument still passes the test, while real `gdbus` exits 1 at once and the helper launches without waiting. Recording `"$@"` one argument per line and comparing the list catches it.
3. When `gdbus` fails for another reason (for example no session bus), the app launches at once but the journal line still says "did not appear within 15s"; "was not available" would be accurate.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducers for optional notes 1 and 2</summary>

# The routing checks in launch-autostart-test.sh read the source text

Reviewed head: f61bc176e9911a67f5dd255a43b2ed3478a55f49

# The test's gdbus fake cannot see argument boundaries; a helper that breaks them passes, and the wait silently disappears

Reviewed head: f61bc176e9911a67f5dd255a43b2ed3478a55f49

In `test/shell.d/launch-autostart-test.sh` the fake `gdbus` (lines 32-40) records `"$*"`, which joins its arguments with spaces, and line 52 compares that one string with `"wait --session --timeout 15 org.freedesktop.Notifications"`. Any change to `bin/omarchy-launch-autostart` that keeps the same words but moves the argument boundaries produces the same string, so the test still passes.

Real `gdbus` rejects those argument lists. For example with `"--timeout 15"` as one argument, GLib's option parser looks for a long option called `timeout 15`, finds none (`parse_long_option` in `glib/goption.c` only accepts `timeout` followed by `=` or the end of the argument), and `handle_wait` in `gio/gdbus-tool.c` prints the usage text and returns failure before it even connects to the bus. `gdbus` exits 1 at once. The helper reads that as a timeout: it logs "did not appear within 15s" and launches immediately, so the wait the PR adds never happens and the start-up race is back, while the PR's test stays green.
